title: Western Ghats eco-sensitive draft and Kerala's exclusion plea
text:
The Union environment ministry reissued the seventh draft notification for an Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) covering the Western Ghats in late July 2026. The draft covers 56,825.7 sq km across six states: Gujarat, Goa, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra and Karnataka. It proposes barring mining, quarrying and sand mining within the ESA, along with new thermal power plants, certain highly polluting industries and large construction projects. Hydel power would be regulated rather than banned, and agriculture and plantations are reported to be unaffected.

The draft is open to public objections for 60 days. The Centre and the six states have not agreed on which villages and areas should be included, a dispute that has continued since earlier drafts. An expert committee set up in 2022 to examine the states' proposals has been given an extension until July 2027.

In September 2026, Kerala's cabinet decided to ask the Centre for the complete exclusion of residential areas and the Cardamom Hill Reserve from the ESA. The state's environment department is to prepare a map of the areas it wants carved out, to be presented to the Union Environment Ministry. The Centre has so far resisted broader exclusions.

questions.q: Which Act is the legal basis under which eco-sensitive zones around national parks and wildlife sanctuaries are notified?
options: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
questions.explanation: Eco-sensitive zones are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, with factors such as biodiversity, proximity to sanctuaries and national parks, and wildlife corridors considered. The other three Acts do not provide the notification basis for these zones.

questions.q: In which year was the Western Ghats inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats received UNESCO World Heritage status in 2012, at the 36th session of the World Heritage Committee in St Petersburg.

questions.q: Which of the six states named in the 2026 draft Western Ghats ESA has the largest area under the draft?
questions.explanation: Karnataka has the largest share of the draft at 20,668 sq km, out of a total of 56,825.7 sq km across six states.

questions.assertion: The Kasturirangan panel's report on the Western Ghats was submitted before the Gadgil panel's report.
questions.reason: The Gadgil panel's report on the Western Ghats was submitted to the Government of India in 2011.
questions.explanation: A is false: the Gadgil (WGEEP) report was submitted in August 2011, and the Kasturirangan report came later, in April 2013. R is true: the Gadgil report was submitted in 2011.

statements: I. Sanjay Kumar headed the Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel.
II. Madhav Gadgil headed the Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel.
questions.explanation: Only II is correct. The WGEEP was headed by Madhav Gadgil. Sanjay Kumar leads the later expert committee formed in 2022, which is separate from the WGEEP.

statements: 1. Goa's share of the 2026 draft Western Ghats ESA is 1,461 sq km.
2. Tamil Nadu's share of the 2026 draft Western Ghats ESA is 6,914 sq km.
3. Kerala's part of the 2026 draft Western Ghats ESA covers 131 villages.
4. Maharashtra's share of the 2026 draft Western Ghats ESA is 17,430 sq km.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Maharashtra's share is 17,340 sq km. Three statements are correct, so the answer is Only three.
